reviewer: Codex provisional creative assessment; not Kevin approval
limits: Scores are subjective assistant judgments, not measured outcomes or approval.
Brand compliance means consistency with this fictional fixture only, not official Xfinity sign-off.
High intensity is not a quality guarantee. Cases include regeneration history, so this is not a controlled causal study.
No research, competitor facts or past campaign results were supplied; rationales must preserve that absence.
Match requestId before reusing these assessments after rerunning an evaluation.

candidates.candidate: When the laptop clocks out, the homework and cartoons are already waiting their turn.
candidates.assessment: Recognizable anthropomorphism; check that taking turns reads as household activity rather than a network limitation.

candidates.candidate: The living room has a shift schedule; the internet is where the handoffs happen.
candidates.assessment: Appropriately understated, but less distinctive and strategically narrow.

candidates.candidate: At home, the baton is usually a tablet with snack crumbs on it.
candidates.assessment: Specific visual surprise fits the handoff spark; Kevin should assess whether the crumb image suits the campaign.

candidates.candidate: The coffee table chairs three committees: work, homework and “what are we watching?”
candidates.assessment: Committee metaphor is playful and usable, though not necessarily more useful than intensity 8.

candidates.candidate: The shared calendar has meetings, math homework and cartoons sharing one tiny Tuesday.
candidates.assessment: Calendar steering appears clearly in a concrete Tuesday scene.

candidates.candidate: The shared calendar is air traffic control for laptops, homework and movie night.
candidates.assessment: Clear response to both controls and steering; air traffic control is a familiar comparison.

candidates.candidate: The shared calendar needs a seating chart for laptops, lessons and movie night.
candidates.assessment: A fresh seating-chart premise under unchanged settings; assess whether it is sufficiently distinct from air traffic control.

candidates.candidate: A shared home has an invisible agenda: meetings, math, and movie night all asking for room.
candidates.assessment: Names negotiation for space without asserting a current trend.

candidates.candidate: Show the tiny heads-ups that make work, homework and watching share a home.
candidates.assessment: Small social behavior fits restrained cultural interpretation.

candidates.candidate: A household’s digital mudroom: everyone brings their online day inside and finds a place for it.
candidates.assessment: Digital mudroom connects a familiar ritual to online life; no retrieved cultural evidence is claimed.

candidates.candidate: Home internet as the family foyer, where each device arrives carrying a different day.
candidates.assessment: Foyer is close to the prior mudroom premise; high intensity did not improve originality here.

candidates.candidate: Think of home internet as the extra calendar square for calls, classwork, and couch time.
candidates.assessment: Calendar image follows steering but the social tension is less clear.

candidates.candidate: When the fridge calendar meets the browser tabs, work, homework, and watching negotiate the day.
candidates.assessment: Fridge calendar and browser tabs create a useful social-negotiation premise.

candidates.candidate: The shared calendar’s secret row: work calls, homework, and couch time penciled in online.
candidates.assessment: Fresh wording under unchanged settings, but the cultural insight remains tentative.

candidates.candidate: Start with the after-work handoff: one person trying to keep everyone’s next thing moving.
candidates.assessment: Person and coordination responsibility now lead; relief is framed as a hypothesis in the rationale.

candidates.candidate: Start with the person fitting work, homework and downtime into the same evening.
candidates.assessment: Clear practical focus; deliberately restrained but fairly generic.

candidates.candidate: Picture the household referee who just wants everyone’s online plans to stop needing a ruling.
candidates.assessment: An unspoken wish gives the adult a stronger point of view; review the referee image for warmth.

candidates.candidate: When the house gets loud, start with the person quietly making room for everyone’s online life.
candidates.assessment: Stronger emotional contrast without claiming the product resolves the emotional burden.

candidates.candidate: Start with the person reading the shared calendar like a traffic map for everyone’s online plans.
candidates.assessment: Follows calendar steering while retaining a human subject.

candidates.candidate: Start with the shared-calendar juggler facing a triple-booked Tuesday of everyone’s online plans.
candidates.assessment: Specific human workload and playful framing; avoid implying this is researched behavior.

candidates.candidate: Start with the person making color-coded calendar chaos feel a little less bossy.
candidates.assessment: New less-bossy-calendar angle; the link to the product is less explicit and may need refinement.

candidates.candidate: Make home internet feel like the handoff point for work, homework, and winding down.
candidates.assessment: Relevant but still close to a generic product-role description; Kevin should push the buying criterion further.

candidates.candidate: Frame Xfinity home internet as the common link across work, homework, and winding down.
candidates.assessment: Clarifies role at low differentiation; low originality is expected but limits usefulness.

candidates.candidate: Evaluate home internet around the handoffs between work, homework, and downtime.
candidates.assessment: Expresses an evaluation criterion without inventing competitor facts.

candidates.candidate: Stop counting devices; start mapping the household handoffs they carry.
candidates.assessment: A concrete shift in the buying question; proposal rather than a substantiated category truth.

candidates.candidate: Let the shared calendar decide what home internet needs to carry.
candidates.assessment: Uses the calendar as an evaluation frame; clarify carry so it cannot imply performance guarantees.

candidates.candidate: Turn the shared calendar’s pileup into a map of what home internet helps connect.
candidates.assessment: Connects steering to an exploration frame; positioning is less sharp than the experimental line.

candidates.candidate: Make the shared calendar the starting lineup for what home internet helps connect.
candidates.assessment: Fresh alternative but drifts toward decorative imagery over a strategic choice.

candidates.candidate: Treat the home like a shared calendar, with internet as the quiet handoff between plans.
candidates.assessment: Rationale names the supplied human-first principle; quiet support is understandable but familiar.

candidates.candidate: Think of home as a shift change, where work, homework and shows take turns online.
candidates.assessment: Taking turns risks suggesting one-at-a-time access; revise before use.

candidates.candidate: Start with the people cueing work, homework and showtime; internet plays stagehand.
candidates.assessment: Clear people-first/technology-supporting-role structure and an explicit supplied principle.

candidates.candidate: Map the day on the fridge door, where work, homework and shows take turns online.
candidates.assessment: Reuses turn-taking and fridge imagery; high pattern exploration did not produce a useful structural departure. Revise before use.

candidates.candidate: Let the shared calendar doodle the day—work, homework, showtime—then invite each plan online.
candidates.assessment: Doodling is a more playful execution of the supplied human-first principle; check clarity.

candidates.candidate: Let the household calendar call roll: meetings, math, movie night—all finding their place online.
candidates.assessment: Responds to steering and keeps activities first, though the roll-call pattern is familiar.

candidates.candidate: When the calendar looks like confetti, let each plan find its online place.
candidates.assessment: Confetti adds a new visual opening under the same configuration; keep the calendar readable and avoid chaos stereotypes.
